findings.source_quotation: Select a given Region only once for a given Command. / Select a given Region only once for a given Special Ability.
findings.expected: Reject repeated Command or SA Region selections before any mutation; retain pending user input. Distinguish permitted multiple options in a single Rally/Build Region from repeated selections.
findings.observed: A durable human plan regions=[Carnutes,Carnutes] passes turn validation and Seizes twice, receiving 8 instead of 4 Forage Resources. Two Entreat entries for Carnutes replace two Belgic Warbands in one SA. Both finish with valid inventories; no correction is requested. findings.title: Rampage forces two Warbands instead of the actor’s chosen quantity

rule.quotation: That target Faction must either remove or Retreat one of its Warbands, Auxilia, and/or Legions (no roll) per Hidden Belgic Warband in the Region that the Belgae flip to Revealed.

findings.source_quotation: That target Faction must either remove or Retreat one of its Warbands, Auxilia, and/or Legions (no roll) per Hidden Belgic Warband in the Region that the Belgae flip to Revealed.
findings.expected: Belgae choose how many Hidden Warbands to flip, bounded by actual available pieces and legal effects; no printed two-Warband cap exists.
findings.observed: The primitive accepts three flips and three target actions. The human dispatcher ignores count/warbands_to_flip data and computes min(2,hidden_belgic,target_pool). With four Hidden Belgic Warbands and four Roman Auxilia, requesting three flips resolves two. Modern CLI asks only Region and target, never quantity. The same mechanism also forces two when a player wants just one. Victim choices are separately audited in BATTLE-RAMPAGE-VICTIM.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Introduce explicit actor flip quantity and current-state validation; preserve a separate target-owned casualty/Retreat request. Apply through ordinary and Event-granted Rampage. Coordinate with BATTLE-RAMPAGE-VICTIM.

findings.expected: Allow one selected Hidden Auxilia to Scout one Warband of each of two factions, and choose Hidden versus already Revealed targets among a faction’s candidates.

findings.title: Human Battle casualty choices can violate mandatory loss priority tiers

rule_source.quotation: If the Faction taking Losses is a Defender who has opted to Retreat, the first Losses taken must be any Allied Tribes and (via die rolls) any Citadel or Fort. In all other cases, any Allied Tribes, Citadel, or Fort may only take Losses after all other pieces of that Faction in the Region have already been removed.

findings.expected: Offer only currently eligible tier, preserving owner choice within that tier and A3.2.4 Settlement/Diviciacus constraints.
findings.observed: With one Arverni Warband and Ally, terminal selects Ally and removes it while Warband survives. Identical choice accepted after pending save/load. Retreating defender can select Warband first while Ally survives. _build_loss_priority only sorts tiers; consult_agent permits any entry.
related_existing_tests: test_diviciacus_loss_legality.py guards Diviciacus but not ordinary static tiers
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Filter legal casualties before exposing options; validate explicit priorities against present legal tier; test Attack/Counterattack, Retreat/non-Retreat, Fort/Citadel/Ally/Settlement and durable invalid input.

findings.title: Ordinary Battle casualties cannot select visibility or physical Allied Tribe

rule_source.quotation: The Faction suffering Losses to its Forces, when an option, chooses which of its own pieces to remove

findings.expected: Offer current physical candidates: Hidden/Revealed/Scouted eligible soft pieces, and each removable Tribe; preserve distinctions in casualty mutation.
findings.observed: One Hidden and one Revealed human Arverni Warband produce two (Warband,None) entries. Durable response for Revealed is rejected as not offered. Two Allied Tribes similarly produce identical (Ally,None); clear_allied_tribe selects sorted candidate. Special Elite/borrowed force identity work does not extend to ordinary humans.
related_existing_tests: test_harassment_decisions.py demonstrates explicit visibility/Tribe choices already exist for Harassment
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add ordinary physical casualty schema and exact Tribe removal; reuse legal tier validation; cover both Attack/Counterattack and save/load/replay.

findings.title: Retreat forces all Hidden defenders and Leader to stay and omits removal-only Retreat

rule_source.rule: Reference Documents/Chapter 3 §3.2.4 Steps 2/6; §3.3.4; Chapter A3 A3.2.4
rule_source.quotation: The Defender must either move all its surviving Leader and Warbands to that Region or remove them. EXCEPTION: The Defender may opt to have any Retreating Leader and/or Hidden Warbands stay put.

findings.expected: Separate declaration from post-Attack surviving-piece disposition; allow legal stay subset against Roman attack, movement of remaining Hidden/Leader, or required removals; no destination should not prevent a legal Retreat declaration.
findings.observed: A base Arverni and an Ariovistus German with 2 Hidden Warbands+Leader each declare Retreat to owned Atrebates. Only one retreat request exists; all 3 pieces stay in Carnutes automatically. With no controlled neighbor, CLI offers only No Retreat and durable true/null is rejected, despite legal Hidden stay/removal outcome.

minimal_reproduction.case: retreat_The Great Revolt; retreat_Ariovistus; retreat_no_destination_cli; retreat_no_destination_session

findings.recommended_repair_scope: Introduce post-Attack survivor disposition request and explicit stay/move/remove quantities. Preserve host promises, scenario restrictions and accepted declaration across pauses. Audit late destination timing separately; this probe does not establish late-control legality.

findings.title: Besiege uses automatic target priority instead of Roman choice

rule_source.quotation: the (Roman) Attacker may automatically remove (Subdue) a Defending Citadel or Allied Tribe (no roll, Attacker’s choice which)

findings.expected: For each chosen Battle, Roman chooses optional eligible Citadel/Ally/Settlement and physical Tribe after relevant state changes, before losses.
findings.observed: Actual Besiege menu selects Region only. Human action with besiege_target=Ally silently removes Citadel and leaves Ally. Saved session logs only voluntary-removal windows for Romans, no Besiege target request. Code always chooses options[0] (Citadel>Ally>Settlement); generic Tribe removal is also automatic.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add typed optional Besiege target/Tribe choice at correct pre-loss boundary; persist/react to current targets; keep at-start Citadel protection and capability exceptions intact.

findings.title: Rampage target cannot choose affected pieces or per-piece removal versus Retreat

rule_source.rule: Reference Documents/Chapter 4 §4.5.2; Chapter A4 A4.5 NOTE
rule_source.quotation: That target Faction must either remove or Retreat one of its Warbands, Auxilia, and/or Legions (no roll) per Hidden Belgic Warband in the Region that the Belgae flip to Revealed.

findings.expected: Victim selects physical pieces and remove/Retreat disposition per affected piece, using one legal destination for those Retreating; Ariovistus automatic Arverni removal remains forced.
findings.observed: Two affected Roman pieces with Hidden Auxilia, Revealed Auxilia and Legion present: only retreat request supplies num_pieces=2 and legal_regions. Choosing remove removes both Auxilia, leaves Legion. No casualty chooser exists. CLI labels are Remove them / Retreat them to destination, preventing mixed dispositions.
related_existing_tests: test_battle.py/command tests do not verify victim physical subset
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Expose victim piece/disposition request; validate exact counts/states, legal shared destination and forced expansion Arverni removal. Coordinate with commands partition actor quantity finding; do not duplicate that cap report.

findings.title: Ordinary March cannot author transit dropoffs

rule_source.quotation: Any of a group’s pieces may drop off in a Region before the rest move on, or split off to move by accompanying Scout

findings.expected: Allow acting faction to specify or reactively choose per-hop dropped physical pieces before next departure/Harassment.
findings.observed: Normal terminal March offers route/count/multiple origin groups only. Supplying details.dropoffs for 1 of 2 Auxilia in Arverni on Provincia→Arverni→Bituriges succeeds but moves both to Bituriges. Standard _execute_march_moves never forwards dropoffs_by_region, although private event-oriented path supports it. Separate origin groups are not a representation of the same carried group and its live casualties.
related_existing_tests: test_cli_march_groups.py tests origin splits, not transit splits
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add standard per-hop dropoff contract/menu or live reactive choice, forward exact selections through existing carried-cohort path; recompute legal quantities after casualties and removal windows. Cross-reference root interruption finding for accompanying Scout.

findings.title: March requires movement and cannot only hide at a selected origin

rule_source.quotation: Origin Region by origin Region, flip all the Marching Faction’s Revealed Warbands there to Hidden; or, for Scouted Warbands, instead remove the Scouted marker and leave them Revealed; then move each Marching group one by one together into an adjacent Region, if desired.

findings.expected: Allow selected paid origin with zero movement, applying mandatory origin flips once; Roman/Gallic/Germanic differences and Frost still apply.
findings.observed: CLI requires one nonempty route. Human Aedui March explicit origin with empty path is invalid March route, rolled back, both Warbands remain Revealed and no Resources spent. _select_affordable_march_moves rejects empty paths and skips zero-piece groups before selecting/billing/flipping origin.
related_existing_tests: test_march_visibility_choices.py origin flipping assumes movement except separate Morasses event
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Represent selected origins independently from moving groups; support hide-only origin selection and charge correctly. Verify no movement, no double flips and exact resume without falsely reporting no effect.

findings.title: Several Event-granted Marches and German guidance still use automatic plans
findings.rule_source_quotation: Card4: "Romans may free March to an adjacent Citadel"; Card17 Tips: "guided by the Romans, not by the Germans Phase sequence"; Cards9,58,65,67,70 and Chapter5 §§5.1/5.4.
findings.expected: The identified human controller chooses origins, destinations, exact participants, optional use and applicable Battle targets.
findings.observed: 4/9/17/58/65/67/70 choose whole groups, routes or destinations internally. The only later requests can be casualties/retreat or a later Command. Card17 probe makes the human Roman executor march Germans into, and Ambush, its own Roman force.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add scoped, actor-owned free-action requests for each printed stage; keep existing heuristics only on explicit defer/NP paths; persist exact cohorts and choices.

findings.title: Fixed Event Battle resolvers suppress human Region or defender selections
findings.rule_source_quotation: Card11: "free Battle there"; Card25: "Free Battle in either Pictones or Arverni Region"; Card36: "Free Battle against a Gallic Faction in 1 Region"; Card45 shaded: "Free Battle against Romans in 1 Region".
findings.expected: The granted battler selects any legal defender, or Region where unfixed, using printed grant constraints.
findings.observed: 11 both profiles and25 choose a defender from priorities;36 unshaded chooses Region/defender by greatest enemy mobile force;45 shaded chooses largest Roman target;70 unshaded chooses default defender after its default March. _plan_fixed_event_battle requests only Diviciacus consent, not a human Battle plan.
minimal_reproduction: probes/base_events_probe.py: automatic_action_70 demonstrates Battle without a Roman plan request; other listed cards statically traced through the same fixed-target helper
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Route fixed Event Battles through a constrained human Battle request; preserve forced targets and event-specific modifiers.

findings.title: Gallic beneficiaries and command order are hardcoded; Remi Influence gives pieces to the wrong faction
findings.rule_source_quotation: 35 shaded: "A Gallic Faction executes 1 Command and 1 Limited Command, in either order";46 shaded: "A Gallic Faction executes a free Command";67: "Romans or a Gallic Faction";68 shaded: "A Gallic Faction with Remi as Ally may ... place a Citadel there with 4 Warbands".
findings.expected: Executor selects a legal beneficiary where offered;35 beneficiary chooses either command order;68 uses Remi-owning Gallic Faction.
findings.observed: 35S and46S always grant executor the actions (even Romans), ignoring supplied faction;35S is always full then Limited.67 always uses executor.68S checks that Remi has some Gallic owner, but places executor pieces; probe Remi=Aedui, executor=Belgae produces Belgic Citadel+4 Warbands.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add explicit beneficiary selection and35 order; derive68 actor from Remi owner and route its optional choice to that seat.

findings.title: Named factions never receive optional Event-effect decisions
findings.rule_source_quotation: 2U: "Romans may shift Senate";18U: "Romans may remove all Germans";23U: "Romans may place Razed marker";26S: "Arverni may remove and place Allies as desired".
findings.expected: Named faction accepts/declines and owns the selections specified in the card, even when another faction executes it.
findings.observed: 2U shifts automatically whenever possible; no decline field.18U/23U execute solely from executor-supplied targets, with no Roman consent.26S executor-supplied removal/placement lists directly alter Allies before the Arverni Rally request. Roman SeatSession probes for2/18/23 finish with pending=null and no inbox answer.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Provide named-faction effect requests with explicit decline, exact targets and source choices. Do not turn absent answers into executor choices.

findings.title: Drought substitutes casualty priorities for every faction’s own selection
findings.rule_source_quotation: Card49 Tips: "Each Faction gets to choose which of its own forces piece ... to remove."
findings.expected: Each human faction independently selects an exact legal piece/Tribe in each Devastated Region, pausing durably before its loss.
findings.observed: Handler removes Roman Legion before Auxilia and Gallic Warband before Ally, without a request. The only override is a Python map keyed by (faction,Region), authored by executor; ordinary JSON string keys are ignored. Roman durable session with Legion+Auxilia loses Legion and has no pending decision.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Implement per-owner casualty requests with JSON-safe exact physical targets, and durable pause/replay between losses; retain printed German priority.

findings.title: Event contracts cannot express smaller quantities or removal-only choices
findings.rule_source_quotation: 3S: "remove 2 Legions";5S: "remove ... 2 Auxilia";19U: "up to 6 ... or ... up to 5";22U: "remove or replace ... up to 4".
findings.expected: Represent exact per-Region quantities, zero-to-maximum choices and removal versus replacement independently.
findings.observed: 3S and5S greedily exhaust first selected Region; cannot remove1+1 if each has2.19U always removes up to maximum from each selected Region or places min(5,Available), ignoring count.22U always replaces if own replacement is Available.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Use explicit entries with count and remove/replace mode; enforce printed totals and leave optional remainder unspent.

findings.title: Several direct Event removals cannot select physical visibility or exact Allied Tribe
findings.rule_source_quotation: Chapter5 §5.1: "executing Faction makes all selections ... such as which pieces are affected";31S: "Remove 3 Allies";45U: "replace up to 2 Arverni Warbands".
findings.expected: Choose exact Hidden/Revealed/Scouted pieces and exact Ally tribe when more than one qualifying counter exists.
findings.observed: 5S/6S/7S/11S/19U/22U/24S rely on remove_piece default Hidden-first.31S accepts Region but no Tribe and clears alphabetically.45U/58U/60U/61U/65S explicitly inspect Hidden then Revealed, excluding Scouted.51S scans states in fixed order. Original6S also removes/replaces Auxilia instead of preserving selected orientation.
minimal_reproduction: probes/base_events_probe.py: litaviccus_ignores_selected_state;litaviccus_scouted_unselectable;cotuatus_tribe_unselectable; remaining listed handlers statically traced
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add exact physical piece state and Tribe fields/menus to direct removals and moves; use state-aware piece helpers and preserve cohort identities.

findings.title: Generated CLI Event schema cannot express several legal handler inputs
findings.rule_source_quotation: Cards6S/11S select Auxilia across Regions;19U offers two literal branches;23U/28/68S select Cities;49 selects owned losses;57S removes Ally/Dispersed.
findings.expected: Typed menu must emit values and collection shapes that the actual handler consumes.
findings.observed: Tuple loops in6S and original11S are missed: schemas are value/regions rather than (Region,count) entries.19 choice is a Region menu so warbands branch is unreachable. City keys23/28/68 use Tribe menus but handlers require City names.49 piece_removals and57 removal become Region strings rather than maps. Accepting NP standard choices can work on some cards but cannot select arbitrary legal alternatives.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Replace lossy inference for these shapes with authoritative per-side schemas and valid literal/City domains. Keep scalar-menu timing separate from this missing-value/shape defect.

findings.title: Human Capability activation/Region choices use unconditional NPC priorities
findings.rule_source_quotation: 10S: "after Ambush may remove defending Fort or Citadel";13U: "Romans choose 1 Region per enemy Battle Command";59U: "Romans may ... in 1 Region";59S: "Each Battle Command ... in 1 Region".
findings.expected: Ask owning human for optional activation or eligible Battle Region, including defensive use and third-party Roman prefire.
findings.observed: 10S always removes Citadel then Fort after Ambush.13U and59U always select greatest Roman Auxilia Region.59S selects first sorted attacking Region or most owner pieces when defending. No human selection request or plan key is consumed.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Create owner-scoped Capability requests at the proper Battle Command/after-Ambush stage with durable persistence; preserve existing defaults only for NPC/defer.

findings.title: Gallic Shouts does not present its private two-card peek
findings.rule_source_quotation: 35U: "Romans may look at the next 2 facedown cards and either execute a free Limited Command or be Eligible."
findings.expected: Present the Roman peek before the action/eligibility decision, with correct privacy.
findings.observed: card_35_roman_peek is only set/cleared. Resolver asks an ordinary free Limited Command with no card identities or card text. Declining that grant DOES yield eligibility, so that outcome is reachable; the confirmed missing feature is the printed information.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Reuse Council private-peek presentation and explicit eligibility choice; do not claim decline cannot reach eligibility. Raw full-state snapshots are not a printed peek UI.

findings.title: Event plan validators accept selections outside printed quantity and target limits
findings.rule_source_quotation: 40U: "3 Warbands, 2 Auxilia, or 1 Ally in each Region";41: "place up to 2 Allies";42U: "up to any 4 ... under Roman Control or up to 2 adjacent";51U: "any 4 Warbands in a Region within 1 of Treveri".
findings.expected: Reject disallowed mixed alternatives, over-quota selections, and out-of-scope targets before committing a human plan.
findings.observed: 40 tracks separate per-type caps allowing both3 Warbands and2 Auxilia in same Region.41 accepts3 Ally placements.42 removes5 Allies on a map with no Roman Control.51U replaces5 Warbands in Provincia (outside Treveri neighborhood). Probes use valid states and legal piece helper operations.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add source-based plan validation for quota, mutually exclusive placement types, target/control and Region restrictions; retain §5.1.3 partial execution only within legal selections.

findings.title: German Allegiances cannot replace Warbands for a Gallic executor
findings.rule_source_quotation: 65S: "remove or replace 5 Germanic Warbands and 1 German Ally with your own (Auxilia for Warbands)".
findings.expected: Gallic executor can replace German Warbands with its own Warbands; Romans use Auxilia; removal-only remains selectable.
findings.observed: Handler always checks/places executing faction AUXILIA after removing each German Warband. A Belgae executor at its own Control loses the German target but receives no Belgic Warband despite ample Available. It also lacks explicit remove/replace and state selection.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Select replacement piece from executor faction and explicit per-piece removal/replacement choice; validate own Control and exact targets.

limitations: Frozen bounded audit. No production/test/rules edits, external sources, balance matrix or broad NPC strategy review.

Every identity/side/profile is enumerated. Numeric cards with one printed text retain a shaded API alias; these are labeled rather than invented as separate source effects. legacy profile resolves by scenario per edition.py and is not a third printed text.
Representative deterministic probes verify shared failure mechanisms; other named subcases carry explicit static trace evidence. No claim that every292 row was independently executed.

Passive capability activation is covered. Ongoing30 Elite and38/O38 consent/physical ownership are cross-reviewed by battle/command partitions;63 Harvest action choices belong to seasonal partition. Q-TRADE-NP-REGION and Q-ELITE-NP-PIECES are pre-existing source questions, not these human gaps.

Generic scalar menus being collected before execution is not by itself reported as missing choice. BE-08 concerns unrepresentable values/shapes; action-window timing repair and entry previews are acknowledged.

Some handlers also under-validate other constraints; BE-11 intentionally freezes at its four verified card families. Scarce-Available ordering for34S/60S/61S/69 is not verified, not asserted defective.
Raw callback None explicitly defers; findings concern no request, ignored explicit legal parameter, invalid schema, wrong actor, or durable session that cannot pause for a request never emitted.
Gallic Shouts eligibility is reachable by declining free Command. BE-10 only confirms missing peek presentation/private decision metadata, not absence of eligibility outcome.
Root owns full-suite run and final integration.

findings.title: Vosegus/Sabis choose human Battles and the optional second Battle with NPC policy
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A21: "Free Battle in a Region within 1 of Sequani. No Retreat. Then, if desired, free Battle there again (Retreat allowed)." A57 substitutes "a Belgica Region". Chapter 5 §5.1 assigns selections to the executing faction.
findings.expected: Executing human selects a legal Region and defender; after the first Battle resolves, selects whether to Battle again and its legal defender. NPC restrictions apply only to NPC seats.
findings.observed: Both sides route directly to _plan_free_battle_command, which calls NPC target scoring and _second_battle_worthwhile. No free-action input is requested. A human Belgae with six Warbands facing two Germans is reported as having no valid target because the chooser only considers Roman Legion losses. Authored battle_plan is ignored. Durable probes completed with no pending choice; all consumed responses were explicit voluntary-removal declines.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Introduce human first/second Battle grants with scope and no-Retreat metadata; preserve the existing NPC planner only for NPC or explicitly delegated choices.

findings.title: A19 shaded uses German NPC movement policy for human play and skips other executors
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A19 shaded: "March all Romans in 1 Region to an adjacent one with Germans. Romans Ineligible through next card."
findings.expected: The executor selects any qualifying origin/destination, including a destination with a Roman Fort or fewer Germans; all Roman mobile pieces March. Any playable faction can execute the side.
findings.observed: Resolver immediately returns for non-German executors. Human Germans receive the NPC no-Fort/outnumber restrictions and automatic best-source selection. An Aedui executor and a German human both fail to move two Auxilia from Sequani to adjacent Ubii containing one German; both Event results report success. No movement choice becomes pending.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Separate human relocation specification from German NPC derivation; validate adjacency/German presence/whole mobile group and preserve compulsory ineligibility.

findings.title: A67 omits the beneficiary and March choices and forces German human NPC Battle policy
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A67: "A Faction other than Arverni may free March into either or both the Nervii or Treveri Regions, then execute a free Command except March in one or both, then flip all friendly pieces there to Hidden."
findings.expected: Choose the receiving non-Arverni faction, optional March groups/routes/destinations, then a legal non-March Command using the resulting board; finally Hide its pieces under §5.1.1.
findings.observed: Grant actor is always the executor. Non-Germans automatically move a largest adjacent group before a generic free Command; Germans run a gather-to-Control-and-Battle-only planner with no human command request. German human with Warbands in Treveri and no enemies completes the Event without a pending choice, although Rally/Raid are available. Schema exposes only flip_hidden_regions, and the handler can apply that hide instruction before movement/Command.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Implement one beneficiary-aware sequential human grant; constrain March destinations and later Command Regions, apply hiding last, retain separate NPC plans.

findings.title: A29 Raid and A69 Ambush targets are auto-derived for humans
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A29 shaded: "Place 4 German Warbands & 1 Settlement among Regions adjacent to Germania. They free Raid." A69 shaded: "If Bellovaci a Belgic Ally, place 6 Belgic Warbands there. They Ambush causing 1 Loss each." Chapter 5 §5.1: "Unless otherwise specified, the executing Faction makes all selections allowed".
findings.expected: Preserve the granted physical force and consult the appropriate human for its legal Raid targets/counts or Ambush defender. Do not infer consent to NPC priorities from selecting Event text.
findings.observed: A29 unconditionally calls derive_raids, which invokes faction NPC planners; human German probe steals two Resources from Romans without a Raid request. A69 chooses max(candidates,piece count); a human Belgic probe asking for Aedui attacks Germans instead, without any target request. The current placement cohort accounting is useful but does not supply the missing choice.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add live scoped target/count grants while preserving actual placed-piece cohorts and existing NPC derivation only on explicit delegation/NPC seats.

findings.title: A20/A58 Roman may-grants are forced or omitted depending on executor
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A20 unshaded: "If Romans within 1 Region of Veneti, they may remove all Arverni from and free Seize there". A58 unshaded: "Romans may free Battle anywhere in Belgica, then free Seize in Belgica".
findings.expected: Romans choose their may-grant when the card is executed by any faction; after acceptance, resolve the printed sequence with chosen legal Battle/Seize actions.
findings.observed: A20 removes Arverni before any Roman acceptance and auto-Seizes/disperses every tribe in Veneti. A58 returns with no grant when the executor is not Romans. For Roman executors A58 auto-chooses Battle and Seizes every Belgica Region with Romans. Durable probes with explicit decline-like unknown Event fields still complete; no actual accept/decline request exists. The unknown fields demonstrate lack of a contract rather than a supported decline syntax.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add a Roman-owned compound optional grant independent of executor, with explicit acceptance and scoped Battle/Seize plans; respect the mandatory remainder only after acceptance.

findings.title: A20/A58 Seize grants run forbidden enemy Rally rolls
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A20 unshaded: "with no rolls for Gallic Rally". A58 unshaded: "with no Harassment or enemy Rally".
findings.expected: Granted Seize suppresses the named Rally effects; A58 additionally suppresses Harassment.
findings.observed: Both resolvers call generic _execute_seize, which always installs _resolve_seize_rally. A58 supplies no_harassment but neither grant suppresses Rally. Seed23 durable probes show four Rally rolls for A20 and six for A58, with substantial Arverni/Belgic placements and extra RNG consumption.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Carry trusted grant-specific Rally suppression into Seize execution and preview; retain ordinary Seize behavior and A58 Harassment suppression.

findings.title: A5 eviction forces the first Home Region and leaves non-Roman structures in Cisalpina
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A5 unshaded: "Only Romans may stack there: non-Romans move their pieces there to their Home Regions or remove them."
findings.expected: Affected non-Romans choose legal Home destination(s) or removal for their pieces, and no non-Roman pieces remain in Cisalpina.
findings.observed: Resolver takes next(first playable Home), never asks for destination/removal, and iterates only Leader/Legion/Auxilia/Warband. German human probe is moved to Sugambri despite a requested Ubii destination and retains an Ally plus Settlement in Cisalpina. Piece census remains balanced, illustrating that conservation alone does not prove legality.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add affected-owner evacuation/removal choices and process all prohibited counters with tribe/pool consistency; keep Roman garrison placement and persistent geography rules.

findings.title: Three explicit up-to effects have no human quantity choice
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference: A40 shaded "for each of up to 3 Regions"; A51 unshaded "remove up to 6 Belgic Warbands there"; A60 unshaded "up to 4 Auxilia there. For each piece not placed, Roman Resources +2."
findings.expected: Executor selects 0..legal maximum, preserving A60 tradeoff between Auxilia and Resources and A51 precise physical removals.
findings.observed: A40 always charges 5 times min(3,eligible Regions); A51 always removes min(6,present) Hidden then Revealed; A60 always places min(4,Available). No quantity parameter is read or exposed. Durable zero-choice attempts drain 15 Resources, remove all six Warbands, and place four Auxilia with no compensating +8 Resources. No relevant request becomes pending.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Provide side-specific bounded quantities/targets with zero as explicit legal selection and reject malformed/ignored choices; include A60 unplaced-piece compensation.

findings.title: Typed human Event plans bypass printed geographic, beneficiary and quantity limits
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference: A29 unshaded "A Gaul or Roman"; A30 unshaded "1 Region within 1 of Sequani"; A36 shaded "2 Settlements and 4 Warbands"; A43 unshaded "2 Arverni Allies and 2 Arverni Warbands within 1 Region of Bibracte"; A45 unshaded "within 1 Region of Intimidated markers".
findings.expected: Validate each card-side complete plan against printed beneficiary, region, type, exact quota/upper bound and current board before committing it.
findings.observed: Public validate_player_action accepts each invalid plan and the durable Event commits it: A29 places five German Warbands as the beneficiary; A30 removes Arverni in distant Morini; A36 places ten German Warbands; A43 replaces three Arverni Warbands in distant Morini; A45 places an Aedui Ally with no Intimidated marker anywhere. Human structure validation returns immediately for Event, and dry-run validation regards handler success as legality.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add shared, side-aware human Event validation with explicit current legality and quota enforcement; terminal options should use those same legal sets. Keep transaction rollback and typed replay stable.

findings.title: A22 shaded Capability never permits the added Intimidating Warband
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A22 shaded: "Intimidate may Reveal 1 added Warband to remove 1 extra piece."
findings.expected: A human with shaded Dread can choose up to three eligible Warbands/removals for Intimidate, subject to available Hidden pieces and ordinary restrictions.
findings.observed: Card only registers Capability. Low-level intimidate accepts only (1,2); execution rejects count>2; both ordinary and timing-aware CLI collectors cap at two. A valid three-Warband probe with Ariovistus and three removable enemies fails with "Intimidate uses at most two Warbands per Region". No shaded A22 consumer was found outside registration/evaluation.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Centralize the Capability-aware Intimidate limit for engine, typed validation and live menus. Check separately how the extra fresh Reveal composes with actual Raid credits without altering adopted rulings.

findings.title: A36 and other removal effects replace human physical-piece selections with fixed priorities
findings.rule_source_quotation: Chapter 5 §5.1: "Unless otherwise specified, the executing Faction makes all selections allowed for in implementing the text, such as which pieces are affected." A36 unshaded: "Remove 2 Settlements and 8 German Warbands total from Morini, Nervii, and Treveri Regions." A17 shaded: "Remove 4 Auxilia from any 1 Region."
findings.expected: Choose exact legal affected counters, including location and visibility when there are more eligible pieces than the required quantity; respect any named actor ownership.
findings.observed: A36 hardcodes Morini,Nervii,Treveri order and Hidden/Revealed priority without a removal parameter; requesting Treveri removes eight Morini Warbands instead. A17 exposes the Region but removes Hidden before Revealed regardless of a visibility selection. The same fixed visibility pattern appears in A5 shaded, A58 shaded and A69 unshaded (static review only); A5 wording additionally names Romans as removers but generic Event params belong to the executor.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Represent physical removals/replacements explicitly (Region, faction, piece type/state, Tribe where needed) with exact required totals and beneficiary-owned requests where the text delegates selection.

findings.title: Remove-all expansion Events leave Scouted Warbands behind
findings.rule_source_quotation: A Card Reference A25 unshaded: "Remove all non-Leader German pieces from Cisalpina." A26 unshaded: "all Arverni Warbands from Sequani and Aedui Regions." A30 unshaded: "Remove all Arverni from 1 Region within 1 of Sequani." A56 unshaded: "Remove all Belgae except Leader from Atrebates Region."
findings.expected: The specified all-piece removals include Scouted Warbands as well as Hidden/Revealed pieces.
findings.observed: Handlers enumerate only (Hidden,Revealed). Four initialized, census-valid durable probes each leave one Scouted Warband in the specified removal region while reporting successful Event execution. This is a deterministic mandatory-effect error, not a missing optional decision.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Use complete visibility classes for mandatory removals and keep all pool/tribe updates correct. Add focused Scouted cases, not a broader NPC policy rewrite.

limitations: Canonical CARD_NAMES_ARIOVISTUS contains exactly 39 A-prefix identities and no C-suffixed key at this commit. All 39 are inventoried exactly without normalization. Carnyx is preserved separately from the printed faction tokens; the only A15C strings in the repository are synthetic test fixtures. CLAUDE.md example A15C does not create an additional current card identity.

No base or 2nd-Edition integer cards and no O38 are included; parent assigned them separately. A38/A63 lingering effects considered only via existing scoped regressions; not a full Interlude cross-product audit.
The 78 entries represent two supported API side flags for each of 39 identities; ten single-text cards have no distinct printed shaded effect.

Supported means reviewed choice path/passive effect with stated focused evidence, not a proof over every state. Not-verified entries deliberately retain untested exact quantities, scarcity/reclamation ordering and physical-selection concerns instead of declaring tests sufficient.

All prepared probes start from a correct empty initialized Ariovistus board and use piece/tribe helpers. validate_state verifies piece conservation, not every stacking/control/Event invariant; A5 demonstrates that distinction.
CLI reachability findings rely on schema/collector/handler traces and focused existing CLI tests. Probes execute durable assistant sessions, not terminal keystroke journeys for every failing card.
No new source ruling or general NPC strategy audit. PR-01–09 preserved; Q-TRADE-NP-REGION and Q-ELITE-NP-PIECES are not reclassified as human defects.

A28 explicit plans and human lending are regression-supported, but omitted human battle_plan still falls through _default_plan (static at cards/admagetobriga.py:181-188); this specific durable omission path was not dynamically probed and is not counted as a separate confirmed finding.

A58 shaded broader Ambush grant scope and A69 exact resident-versus-placed participation require additional work if desired; this partition freezes them at inspected evidence and does not expand scope.
No full-game/balance matrix or fresh full suite run; root owns the mandatory full pytest and documentation commit.

findings.title: Interlude force reductions and Cisalpina relocations bypass human owners
findings.rule_source: A Scenario - The Gallic War, Adjust Forces
findings.source_quotation: Player and Non-player Factions adjust Forces in order as follows. Remove or replace pieces in Home Regions last, otherwise selecting Regions desired ... Remove at least the fraction indicated ... Factions in the above order relocate their Forces from Cisalpina to Home Regions (Ally to Subdued Tribe only) or remove them.
findings.expected: Prompt each controlling human in order, including Germans choosing Arverni Forces; allow minimum-or-more removals, exact physical pieces, permitted Tribe replacements and Cisalpina Home destinations/removal.
findings.observed: All five reductions use random/first-target/minimum algorithms. Germans use Available Warbands first for the fifteen permanent removals. Cisalpina always removes every piece. Only Ambiorix/Caesar destination ties have an owner request. Durable German reduction and Roman Cisalpina probes complete with zero accepted choices and no pending request; all resulting states validate.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add staged owner-authored reduction/replacement/relocation requests with per-step legality, amount minima, Home-last constraints, physical cohorts, German ownership of Arverni step, and frontend durable replay. Keep bot algorithms as explicit/default NP paths.

findings.title: Roman Interlude expedition and marker-preservation choices are unreachable in human sessions
findings.rule_source: A Scenario - The Gallic War, Britannia Expedition and Spring
findings.source_quotation: Romans choose whether to conduct a 54BC Britannia expedition ... another 3 or more Legions, and 1 or more Auxilia ... Romans may keep one Dispersed or Dispersed-Gathering marker as is.
findings.expected: Roman chooses expedition/decline, exact origins and allowed quantities, then optional one marker preservation; pending input blocks completion.
findings.observed: Raw kwargs expose conduct and preservation only. play_card invokes resolve_winter_card(state) without these kwargs and no reactive request is emitted. Expedition code ignores all dict fields except conduct and always takes the first three further Legions and one Auxilia. Durable initialized Gallic War Interlude conducts automatically with decision_source=np, preserves no marker and logs zero human choices.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add Roman-owned staged expedition and preservation requests with exact physical selection, decision previews, legality and transactional persistence; wire both frontends through common engine requests.

findings.title: Pax first-Harvest Legion placement is automatically concentrated in one Region
findings.rule_source: Scenario - Pax Gallica, During the 1st Winter Round; Gallic War Second Half
findings.source_quotation: At the start of that Harvest Phase, the Romans place the three Legions from the Winter Track into any Belgica Region(s).
findings.expected: Roman selects distribution of the available track Legions across any legal Belgica Regions.
findings.observed: winter.py selects a single max-Roman-piece Region and places all k Legions there with no request/parameter. Durable first-Winter probe accepts one quarters_plan, then completes without a Harvest choice and puts all three at Atrebates.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Add exact Region/count request before Harvest track placement; apply also first post-Interlude Winter when track Legions remain; preserve fixed NP priority only for NP or explicit default.

findings.title: Human Belgae starts The Great Revolt with the wrong Leader
findings.rule_source: Scenario - The Great Revolt, Players and Victory
findings.source_quotation: If a player is running only the Belgae, or if a single player is running the Romans and Aedui, at setup flip the Belgic Successor to Ambiorix.
findings.expected: A single human Belgae seat starts with Ambiorix. Paired ownership must also inform the printed alternate trigger.
findings.observed: setup always places Successor; frontends assign human modes afterward without the adjustment. Real llm_seat init --seat Belgae saves Successor at Sugambri, with no state-validation error.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Make scenario setup depend on explicit player ownership/seat configuration and apply/replay the mandatory Leader flip. Single-seat Belgae trigger is independently repairable before broader paired-player support.

findings.title: Quarters cannot select which visibility cohort relocates
findings.source_quotation: They may relocate any such pieces to any adjacent Regions ... The Romans may relocate any Legions, Auxilia, and Roman Leader on the map ...
findings.expected: Owner selects exact Hidden/Revealed/Scouted Warbands/Auxilia and counts while preserving visibility.
findings.observed: Four-item relocation tuple has no physical-state field; allocation consumes Hidden then Revealed then Scouted. Probe with 3 Hidden+1 Revealed moves one Hidden; a five-item tuple selecting Revealed is rejected. This can matter during Uprising/after-Harvest Campaign before Spring hides all pieces.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Extend relocations and Provincia continuation to explicit physical-state cohorts, update count menus/validators and original-piece allocation; preserve legacy count-only plans with documented defaults.

findings.title: Resource-transfer choices are limited to one early outgoing CLI gift and omit legal Winter/incoming windows
findings.source_quotation: A Faction may transfer Resources ... during either’s execution ... of a Command or Event ... Factions may transfer any Resources ... during the Quarters and Harvest Phases.
findings.expected: Permit legal gifts by either involved faction during action and by any eligible faction in Quarters/Harvest, with legal amounts/recipients and owner authority.
findings.observed: Only acting faction gives, at action start. CLI offers one recipient and amounts 1..min(stock,12), despite no 12 cap. Durable supports multiple outgoing gifts but has no incoming/Winter request. QUESTIONS already acknowledges missing Winter transfers and one recipient; 12 cap and during-other-party window remain visible restrictions.
findings.minimal_reproduction: probes/winter_setup_probe.py; output probes/winter_setup_probe.json#transfer_cli; inspect executor/Quarters schema for absent other-giver and Winter slots

findings.observed: At an actual NP Aedui refusal d000002, {replacement:{command:Recruit,sa:No SA,details:[1]}} raises AttributeError at details.get. SeatSession catches only ValueError/TypeError, so consult_agent converts the exception to raw None fallback and the engine continues with the original Recruit. In the full Command probe a later voluntary-removal window finally interrupts and rolls back, but the pending request is now voluntary_removal with the same d000002 and the malformed queue entry remains. Isolating the actual engine-authored reconsideration boundary returns the original plan without an accepted response; finish clears pending. This reproduction does not demonstrate an irrevocably committed full Command.
